messages:
anya: Quick heads-up — Orchid v2 int8 onboard shows a regression on mixed CJK+RTL samples.

riley: repro steps?

anya: Ran the standard locale-sample set with vertical substrings, batch 16, seq 512. Baseline float BLEU=29.2, int8=25.0. Dump attached snippet:

```text
input: "（中文） مرحبا kanji漢字​"   # mixed CJK + Arabic + zero-width
baseline: "你好، ... 漢字"
orchid-int8: "你好، ..."
``` 

samir: That's a solid drop. Any tokenization diffs? char counts?

anya: Token counts differ on zero-width + katakana sequences. Tokenizer produces 3 extra tokens in int8 path compared to float. Also we see stray ZWJ merging with punctuation.

jeff: Could this be a preprocessing nondeterminism in quantized tokenizer kernel? Any difference in normalization flags set when exporting the int8 build?

xiao: I noticed our int8 build uses a fast C++ tokeniser with `-O3` flags and a patched ICU fallback. Might be a normalization table mismatch.

ml-ci-bot: CI eval job #orchid-int8-5234 completed: overall BLEU change -4.1, failure rate 12%. See /ci/artifacts/5234.

riley: Action items: (1) bisect to preprocessing commit (anya), (2) run tokenizer parity script vs float on 5k mixed samples (samir), (3) test with ICU fallback disabled (xiao). I'll kick a small canary with normalization flags toggled after (1).

anya: On it. I'll start bisect now and post minimal repro if found. :mag:

jeff: If it's normalization, quick fix might be to pin unicode normalization stage to NFKC for int8 build and re-export. Keep me posted.

samir: I'll run tokenizer parity later today and post token diff samples.

anya: thanks — will update in this thread.
